title: Around prompt 40 your AI forgets what you're building, and GitHub's fix just crossed 110,000 stars
description:
Somewhere around prompt 40 your AI forgets what you're building and starts breaking its own code. GitHub's fix for that just crossed 110,000 stars.

Spec Kit is GitHub's own open source toolkit for spec driven development. Instead of throwing vague prompts at Claude Code, you write a spec first, and that spec becomes the single source of truth your AI answers to. Four phases: specify describes what you're building, plan drafts the full architecture, tasks breaks it into small atomic steps, implement ships code against the spec. Nothing moves forward until the phase before it validates. It plugs into more than 30 tools, including Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex and Windsurf.

Honest part: day one feels slower, because you're writing documents while everyone else is already prompting. Day ten, their project is a pile of patches and yours still ships. Most builders are shipping vibes. You'll be shipping specs.
